FP&A scope note

This version tailors the enterprise dashboard for a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis. It keeps workforce and position-control data, but the primary read is fiscal: actuals vs. plan, position-control economics, endowment and sponsored-research funding exposure, and 2-year scenario modeling. Figures remain synthetic planning assumptions for portfolio design, not official Harvard payroll or finance records.
FP&A calendar architecture

Default workflow mirrors how financial planning work actually happens

Instead of asking a director to hunt through HR-style tabs, the landing path is organized by current-month variance, mid-year recalibration, and multi-year budget formulation.

Tier 1 · Current MonthActive Variance Ledger: actuals, commitments, funded positions, ICR yield, salary/fringe run-rate, and owner-ready exceptions.
Tier 2 · Q2 RecalibrationMid-Year Review Sandbox: actuals + projected run-rates to June 30, vacancy savings rules, and funding-source reliability tests.
Tier 3 · 5/10/15/20-Year PlanningMulti-Year Budget Formulation Engine: long-range structural sustainability, Corporation-approved endowment smoothing indexes, structural-deficit testing, merit/fringe assumptions, and soft-money cliff risk.
Unified FP&A operating model

One recommended decision path, not separate pro/con options

This combined layer presents the FP&A Director role as one integrated operating contract: fiscal lifecycle discipline, research-school finance complexity, enterprise data governance, and human-owned predictive planning all feed the same decision path.

4:4:4 decision-path layout
1 · Fiscal lifecycle
3 tiers
Current-month active variance ledger, Q2 recalibration sandbox, and 5/10/15/20-year budget formulation are treated as one planning cycle.
2 · Funding reliability
T1/T2/T3
Every position, project, and operating line is tagged by core base, unrestricted operating, or volatile / soft-money exposure before commitments are treated as recurring.
3 · Academic economics
NTR + ICR
Space economics, recharge centers, net tuition, stipend match, ICR yield, global subrecipient risk, and debt service are modeled inside the same forecast.
4 · Data contracts
API gate
Zod / Pydantic-style schema checks quarantine malformed rows, invalid object codes, duplicate keys, and negative budget values before dashboard serialization.
5 · Audit integrity
MAPE + RLS
Forecasts carry scorecards, immutable fiscal snapshots, k<5 suppression, row-level security, and human signoff before leadership use.
6 · Inter-entity economics
Multi-tub
Cross-department tuition and program-cost allocation, joint appointments, fractional ICR splits, and shared-program cost rules are governed as financial architecture, not side agreements.
7 · Macro reserve control
Stress test
Endowment payout shocks, federal funding shifts, inflation, FCI/deferred maintenance, and unrestricted reserve-floor thresholds are built into scenario gates.
8 · Portfolio diplomacy
Adoption
Fully allocated academic margins, program lifecycle choices, and shadow-system change management are handled through faculty-facing, non-hierarchical governance.
9 · Recruiting streams
ARIeS / ATS
Academic searches and administrative requisitions feed the same payroll forecast through governed start-date, vacancy, and recruitment-timing interfaces.
10 · Salary quadrant
4 baselines
Advertised range, budget salary, current salary, and forecast salary are reconciled through business-rationale workflows instead of flat script overrides.
11 · Cyclic memory
3Y avg
Seasonal spikes from fall launch, Q2 recalibration, and year-end close are normalized with rolling historical overlays before executive escalation.
12 · Blocker rules
No silent 0s
Missing files, blank joins, unmapped keys, and stale extracts trigger data-quality exceptions rather than disappearing from Chan School forecasts.

Macro-institutional strategy layer now embedded in the same path

  • Inter-entity friction: reconcile Chan cross-department tuition and program-cost sharing, joint-faculty cost sharing, cross-program registration flows, and fractional ICR before treating program revenue as locally available.
  • Capital asset drag: connect Facility Condition Index, deferred maintenance, lab equipment lifecycle, and reserve requirements to the recurring operating forecast.
  • Macro stress testing: simulate endowment payout reductions, federal grant sequestration, inflation shocks, tuition elasticity shifts, and unrestricted reserve-floor breaches.
  • Academic portfolio economics: audit centers, departments, certificates, and degree pathways with fully allocated costs, mission value, space use, central overhead, and IT fractions.
  • Change governance: translate technical controls into academic diplomacy so department chairs, PIs, faculty leaders, DFAs, and central partners adopt one trusted planning standard.

Operational workflow layer now embedded in the same path

  • Parallel recruiting pipelines: reconcile ARIeS academic searches and Careers@Harvard / administrative ATS requisitions into one position-control forecast with explicit start-date and vacancy-timing assumptions.
  • Salary variance quadrant: explain the difference among advertised hiring range, approved budget salary, current incumbent salary, and forecast run rate without overwriting valid historical records.
  • Cyclic baseline memory: apply a three-year rolling historical overlay to separate true structural deficits from Q1 fall-launch spikes, Q2 endowment smoothing adjustments, and Q4 grant-transfer acceleration.
  • Data-validation blockers: convert blank source files, unmapped joins, and missing operational feeds into visible data-quality exceptions rather than silent zeros or hidden exclusions.

Combined recommended action path

  • Start with the variance signal: identify whether the issue is structural salary pressure, temporary coverage, timing savings, grant/restriction exposure, inter-entity allocation friction, capital drag, reserve-floor pressure, recruiting-system timing risk, salary-baseline mismatch, seasonal noise, or silent data failure.
  • Validate the source: run API/schema checks, ARIeS vs. Careers@Harvard / ATS feed reconciliation, central-to-local reconciliation, immutable FY snapshot comparison, and source-owner confirmation before escalating numbers.
  • Normalize the baseline: compare advertised hiring range, budget salary, current salary, and forecast salary; then apply a three-year cyclic overlay so Q1, Q2, and Q4 seasonality does not look like a structural trend.
  • Classify the funding: assign Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 reliability, separate restricted from flexible funds, and require bridge plans for soft-money cliff lines.
  • Reconcile Chan department/center economics: normalize tuition splitting, joint appointments, Chan center/department ICR sharing, cross-program registration flows, and shared-program costs before assigning local margin.
  • Apply academic-finance controls: test ICR yield, wet/dry lab cost-per-square-foot, recharge-rate compliance, net tuition elasticity, global subrecipient exposure, internal lending impact, FCI exposure, and deferred-maintenance burden.
  • Stress-test sustainability: model endowment payout shocks, federal funding shifts, inflation, tuition elasticity, reserve-floor breaches, equipment obsolescence, and fully allocated academic portfolio margins.
  • Decide through governance: use blocker rules for blanks/unmapped joins, MAPE / C-index scorecards, k<5 privacy suppression, RLS-gated drill-through, human-in-the-loop review, and academic-diplomacy adoption gates; no automated staffing, funding, portfolio, or policy decisions.

Plain-language executive recommendation

  • Use the dashboard as a single FP&A control tower: the same signal should show the number, source reliability, methodology, risk owner, governance checkpoint, and next action.
  • Use recommendation logic: action, rationale, risk control, expected result, and decision gate.
  • Keep the detailed methodology available as reference, but the landing page should remain executive-readable and action-oriented.

Sponsored Research Lifecycle DrawerOpens only when needed: federal fringe true-ups, capped indirects, salary cap exposure, and bridge-funding decisions tied to the Funding Reliability Matrix.
Research lifecycle
DHHS negotiated fringe true-upsModel provisional vs. finalized fringe-rate variance as an FY+2 budget lag, not a current-year surprise.
  • Signal: provisional rate differs from final negotiated rate.
  • Action: hold a fringe reserve or reforecast sponsored payroll loads before renewal packages are released.
Foundation capped indirectsWhen sponsors cap indirect cost recovery, the shortfall becomes an unrestricted subsidy unless direct-charge-eligible support is budgeted correctly.
  • Signal: non-federal awards below institutional recovery target.
  • Action: review admin computing, data storage, specialized support, and project-management lines at proposal stage.
Federal salary overage isolationSalary above sponsor cap should be isolated from FC40 award spending and mapped to approved unrestricted or designated support.
  • Signal: NIH salary cap exceeded.
  • Action: split allocation before payroll posting, not after audit review.
Bridge-funding runway verificationExpiring Tier 3 awards should not be treated as recurring base support until renewal, bridge, or shutdown plans are confirmed.
  • Signal: award expires within 6 months.
  • Action: freeze local vacancy-savings reallocations until bridge runways are verified.
Decision this drawer supportsCan the unit safely spend, hire, or reallocate against this sponsored-research funding stream?
Evidence neededRate agreement, award end date, sponsor cap rule, direct-charge justification, bridge memo, and source-owner signoff.
Leadership actionApprove, hold, bridge, reclassify, or escalate to research administration before budget assumptions become commitments.

🎯 FP&A Director Diagnostic Mandate

As a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis, the expectation is a unified fiscal diagnostic tool linking position control, recruiting pipelines, funding source reliability, seasonal baseline memory, and operating variance to institutional sustainability. This view focuses on budget impact, revenue-to-expense run rate, payout smoothing, ICR yield, vacancy savings, salary-quadrant reconciliation, data-validation blockers, and soft-money exposure in one governed planning layer.
>45 daysService request aging threshold requiring escalation review.
100.2%Workforce payroll tracking against budget.
23.5%Critical skills gap exposure across role families.
+18%Escalated casework volume rising year-over-year.

Tab 1 Core FP&A expectations

  • Identify cross-tub budget variance and funding-source friction before year-end.
  • Forecast year-end salary/fringe burn using funded-position and payroll velocity models.
  • Flag payroll, fringe, endowment payout, and ICR deviations before they become structural pressure.
  • Show DEIB metrics only as aggregate, privacy-compliant leadership signals.
  • Separate temporary vacancy savings from recurring base-budget capacity.

Tab 2 Immediate FP&A concerns requiring attention

  • Service request aging exceeding the 45-day threshold.
  • Workforce payroll tracking at 100.2% of budget.
  • Critical skills gap of 23.5% in technology and adjacent roles.
  • Escalated casework volume rising 18% year-over-year.

Tab 3 Revenue & funding alignment needed

  • Endowment payout dependency modeling for long-term commitments.
  • Sponsored research funding tracking to isolate soft-money role exposure.
  • Vacancy savings reallocation rules directing capital to university priorities.

Tab 4 Institutional strategy & policy data needed

  • AI deployment headcount-impact forecasting for automation role transitions.
  • Cross-school talent mobility tracking for internal pipelines.
  • Federal grant compliance scoring for regulatory exposure.
  • Academic initiative mapping aligning staffing to future research priorities.

Executive Summary

FY2026 — Harvard Chan School Highlights

Service request aging is the near-term pressure point. The synthetic median approval cycle is 7.8 weeks, with 46 records over the 45-day threshold. Weekly aging review is recommended for approvals, role changes, and hiring records.
Control and role-change packets are mostly on track. 86% of active packets are complete or on schedule, but 14 need final evidence, owner, or approval-route confirmation before leadership review.
Business partner engagement is a positive signal. Onboarding, manager enablement, and professional-development participation are modeled at 76%, supporting a repeatable FY2027 service-readiness dashboard.
Finance-linked planning matters. Approval timing, leave coverage, salary/classification flags, and open roles are translated into budget, service-continuity, and policy-risk decisions for Chan School leadership.

Weighted Multi-Factor Attrition Forecast (WMAF) — 12-month horizon

1) Current unit headcountHᵢ = filled headcount in Chan School department/center/program i. This keeps the forecast tied to operating scale.
2) Weighted historical base rateαᵢ = 0.5×FY26 voluntary + 0.3×FY25 voluntary + 0.2×FY26 involuntary. This isolates addressable risk from one-year noise.
3) Known retirement pipelineR₁₂ = count of active employees meeting Rule of 65/70 or documented retirement notifications within 12 months.
4) Climate / workload adjustmentC₁₂ = roles in units with engagement score <65 × 0.15. This adds an explicit stress-signal adjustment.

ETOB-ready mission economics layer

Map every dollar to mission, program lifecycle, grant capacity, and sustainable revenue growth.

This section generalizes the FP&A Director dashboard for any school, center, department, or administrative portfolio. It keeps the existing position-control, budget, and funding-risk architecture, then adds the executive bridge: how money connects to mission, academic programs, research centers, service centers, digital learning, sponsored awards, restricted funds, and revenue-growth decisions.

How to read this section: the goal is not to make finance separate from mission. The goal is to give deans, DFAs, department chairs, research leaders, center directors, and program owners a common operating map: what should be scaled, redesigned, sunset, subsidized intentionally, converted into a sustainable income engine, or strengthened for grant competitiveness.

Revenue & Grant Growth Engine — General School / Department Playbook
Executive use: this block separates growth options that create flexible revenue from grant actions that protect sponsored-research recovery. Each card is reusable for Chan School departments, research centers, education programs, service units, and administrative offices.
Flexible revenue

Professional / executive education growth

Package faculty expertise into short courses, certificates, summer institutes, custom cohorts, and employer-sponsored learning with a margin floor.

Enrollment scale

Hybrid, online, and stackable credentials

Convert high-demand content into modular offerings that grow net tuition while avoiding new space-heavy fixed costs.

Service-center income

Recharge centers, labs, museums, and analytics cores

Use compliant internal rates while monetizing excess capacity for external users, affiliates, clinical partners, or sponsored collaborations.

Gift-to-operating fit

Restricted fund alignment & donor-funded priorities

Map donor terms to eligible recurring costs, seed funding, matching pools, and strategic initiatives so flexible core funds are released safely.

Grant capture

Sponsored award pipeline expansion

Build a proposal pipeline by sponsor, PI / faculty cluster, due date, probability, required match, facilities impact, and recovery rate.

Grant protection

Indirect-cost, cost-share, and renewal defense

Protect the school from hidden subsidies by validating ICR, direct-cost attribution, cost share, renewal risk, bridge plans, and closeout residuals.

Programmatic Lifecycle — Past, Current, Future

1. Retrospective analysis

Audit closed or sunset initiatives to recover value, resolve deficits, and build evidence for future pricing and portfolio decisions.

  • Grant closeout residual capture.
  • Legacy deficit resolution velocity.
  • Alumni ROI and placement-yield evidence.

2. Active optimization

Monitor live programs, research centers, and field initiatives for variance, reallocation options, and cost-recovery exposure.

  • Faculty salary coverage run-rate.
  • F&A / ICR yield versus negotiated or capped rates.
  • Marginal operational cost per student.

3. Predictive strategy

Model pipelines and launch costs before commitments become structural budget pressure or soft-money cliffs.

  • Grant application pipeline velocity.
  • Enrollment funnel conversion elasticity.
  • Faculty startup package amortization.

Strategic Income Generation Blueprint — Five Revenue Vectors
Unrestricted growth

Executive education & B2B public-health training

Build high-margin professional programs for health-system, biopharma, corporate wellness, and ministry-of-health audiences.

Sponsored research protection

Non-federal indirect cost recovery optimization

Where sponsors cap indirects, shift eligible administrative, computing, storage, and specialized support costs into direct-cost budgets.

Service-center monetization

Core facilities & high-demand service centers

Use cost-recovery compliance for internal academic users while pricing excess external capacity at market rate.

Scalable margin

Low-marginal-cost digital learning

Model asynchronous or hybrid MPH / credential expansion where instructional-design investment creates repeatable global capacity.

Restricted-fund fit

Gift matching & endowment resource thawing

Map restricted criteria to eligible recurring expenses, freeing flexible core dollars without violating donor terms.

Operational Heuristics — Formula Logic for the Five Revenue Vectors
Executive Education & B2BNet Unrestricted Contribution Margin = Gross Program Revenue − (Faculty Overload Pay + Fractional Direct Delivery Overhead + Central Tub Assessment)Use as the program-entry test before custom cohorts enter the annual plan.
Non-Federal ICR OptimizationDirect Attribution Yield = (Admin Salaries Reclassified as Direct Costs + Dedicated Server/Data Storage Direct Lines) ÷ Total Proposal BudgetProtects the core budget when foundations cap indirect recovery.
Dual-Tier Core FacilitiesCommercial Core Profit Margin = External Market Rate Asset Charge − (Compliant Base Cost + Depreciation Reserve Surcharge)Separates internal compliance rate logic from external market pricing.
Digital Learning ScaleDigital Cohort Net Income Elasticity = (Enrollment Volume × Digital Tuition Rate) − (Fixed Instructional Design Amortization + Scale-Variable Grader Cost)Tests whether online growth creates durable margin after student support is priced.
Gift / Endowment ThawingCore Cash Released = Σ(Recurring Operating Expenditures matching Restricted Gift Criteria) → Reallocate Unrestricted Funds to ReservesRequires donor-purpose metadata, controller review, and audit-ready mapping.

Scale nowExecutive education, digital learning, and external service-center capacity can produce flexible income when faculty capacity, market demand, and pricing controls are validated.
Redesign before scalingNon-federal grants and low-ICR foundation awards need cost-policy review before they become hidden subsidies against the core operating budget.
Thaw carefullyRestricted gifts and endowment payout should be mapped to eligible recurring expenses only with donor-purpose documentation and controller review.
Do not automatePortfolio decisions are human-governed: AI can summarize, forecast, and flag risk, but deans, finance, research administration, and program leaders own final action.
Decision Workflow — From Program Evidence to Budget Action
Inventory the portfolioClassify each degree, center, field program, service center, and digital product by lifecycle stage and funding source.
Attach measurementsBind margin, mission impact, ICR yield, salary coverage, student cost, and pipeline probability to each program.
Route the decisionAssign each program to scale, optimize, sunset, protect, subsidize intentionally, or hold for additional evidence.
Fund the planUse recurring-only funds for recurring commitments; treat one-time gifts, reserves, and expiring grants as non-base resources.

Equipment Lifecycle Capital Reserve Logic

Specialized assets such as sequencing platforms, mass spectrometers, cryogenic imaging systems, and high-performance computing nodes require a compliant recharge model that funds replacement over time without treating forward-looking replacement cost as a simple direct charge to active federal awards.

Equipment replacement surcharge rate:
Replacement Surcharge = (Estimated Future Replacement Asset Cost − Accumulated Linear Historical Depreciation) ÷ Projected Billable Equipment Utilization Hours over Lifespan

Comprehensive FP&A Strategy Framework — Final Operating Architecture
1. Macro-strategy coreETOB negotiation, endowment payout smoothing, and multi-tub revenue-sharing parameters.
2. Operational pillarsPosition control, parallel ATS / ARIeS timing, NIH cap leakage, and fund-class validation.
3. Mission economics vectorRevenue and grant growth blueprints, lifecycle classifications, and mission-to-margin measurement.
4. Asset / grant engineeringStartup J-curves, bridge gates, grant renewals, depreciation reserves, and cross-registration net revenue flows.
Specialized Data Validation Contracts — Revenue & Grant Ingestion Guardrails
Unmapped Sponsoring Entity QuarantineAny grant record with a missing foundation code, sponsor type, or overhead parameter routes to a data-quality holding queue rather than defaulting to 0% overhead.
Conditional Null Space-Planning LogicIf lab square footage is missing, the model assigns the highest local utility run-rate and alerts the facility owner instead of silently omitting allocated space cost.
Human-in-the-Loop Revenue FencesPredictive models can rank grant win probability and enrollment elasticity, but tuition, faculty startup, funding, and staffing actions require formal human approval.
Small-Cohort Privacy SuppressionProgram and workforce views suppress personally identifying small cohorts before leadership summaries are released.

Executive Proposal — Integrating Mission Economics into the Multi-Year Financial Plan

  1. Architectural mandate under ETOB fiscal parameters: evaluate every funded line, position-control allocation, and space commitment through a Funding Reliability Matrix across stable core funds, flexible operating bases, and volatile soft-money streams.
  2. Intentional margin expansion: coordinate five revenue strategies — executive education, direct-cost attribution, dual-tier cores, digital learning scale, and restricted-fund fit — to reduce structural deficit exposure without weakening the mission.
  3. Governance and data resilience: enforce validation passes, data lineage, small-cohort suppression, and human ownership of all final employment, funding, program, and structural decisions.

1. Advanced modeling rigor
  • Replace deterministic WMAF attrition heuristics with Cox Proportional Hazards or Random Survival Forests.

2. Model validation metrics
  • Expose MAPE for payroll forecast accuracy.
  • Expose C-index for attrition-risk sorting quality.
  • Show backtest window, training window, refresh date, drift status, and owner signoff.
3. Feature engineering
  • Add Boston-Cambridge-Newton CPI-U and local wage-premium vectors.
  • Engineer market-pressure signals for technology, finance, HRIS, analytics, and research-support roles.
  • Create funding-risk features for sponsored research and soft-money roles.

4. Advanced privacy infrastructure
  • Move beyond small-cell suppression into k-anonymity and l-diversity checks across intersecting filters.

  • Explore differential privacy for executive DEIB summaries using calibrated noise.
5. Visualization + UI architecture
  • Replace radar comparisons with linear dot/bar comparisons and explicit target bands.
  • Use fluid chart wrappers with aspect-ratio containers instead of hardcoded mobile-breaking heights.

Operational Drill-Down — Position-Level Budget vs. Forecast Payroll · Filled vs. Open/Pending

Why grade range, budget salary, current salary, and forecast salary may not match

The advertised salary grade/range is the compensation reference band for a posted role. The dashboard fields are planning fields: budget salary reflects the approved position-control budget, current salary reflects the incumbent or last-filled payroll value, and forecast salary reflects expected start date, merit/adjustment, vacancy savings, and bridge assumptions. A mismatch should trigger reconciliation, not automatic correction.
Raw rows for export and review are split into Filled / Active and Open / Pending groups so finance partners can separate committed payroll from vacancy, search, start-date, and bridge assumptions. Use the Shortlist button on each row to view synthetic candidate names, selection comments, and whether the row reflects an internal hire, external hire, or pending selection. In a live implementation, shortlist fields should be sourced from the authorized recruiting system for the role type — ARIeS for academic searches where applicable and the administrative ATS / Careers@Harvard workflow for staff searches. Executive Briefing Memorandum — FP&A Watch Items and Sponsored-Research Runway

Purpose. This brief summarizes the management decisions suggested by the current FP&A dashboard signals. The goal is not to debate every chart, but to confirm which budget, staffing, and sponsored-research items require a hold, bridge, reforecast, or escalation before the next review cycle.

While the overall salary and fringe run-rate is tracking close to plan at 100.2% of budget, the Tier 3 volatile soft-money matrix flags $42.7M in expiring awards over the next six months. I recommend freezing local vacancy-savings reallocations until bridge-funding runways, renewal status, and sponsor restrictions are verified.
  • Immediate decision: confirm whether expiring sponsored-research lines may continue to support salary commitments, or whether those lines require bridge funding, phased hiring, or slow-spend controls.
  • Budget action: separate recurring payroll pressure from timing savings, open requisition delays, and temporary coverage assumptions before releasing local vacancy savings.
  • Compliance action: review DHHS fringe true-ups, foundation capped indirects, NIH salary-cap overages, and CAS/direct-charge assumptions before budget relief is booked.
  • Operating action: assign one owner to each high-risk exception and require source evidence, due date, and closeout status within the 90-day impact baseline.

Recommended next step. Approve a short hold on discretionary reallocations for affected units, route the sponsored-research lifecycle checks to FP&A and Research Administration, and return with a clean list of release/hold/bridge decisions.

Recommended meeting script

1
Ask for decisions, not reactions.“Which of these items can we close this week, and which need leadership authority?”
2
Assign one owner per risk.Each signal must leave the meeting with owner, due date, evidence file, and next checkpoint.
3
Separate structural from timing noise.Payroll and grant signals should not become base-budget decisions until timing, vacancy, and coverage effects are isolated.
4
Suppress curiosity-only charts.If a visual does not change an owner, due date, decision, or risk route, keep it in evidence / methodology view.

What the reader should take away

  • Do first: close the named readiness and approval gaps before executive review.
  • Decide next: whether payroll variance is recurring budget pressure or timing / coverage pressure.
  • Escalate: policy exceptions and delayed searches that block continuity.
  • Do not over-read: AI/ML and priority charts are supporting evidence, not the answer.

Reviewer checklist before publish

  • Reject rows with invalid tub/fund class combinations or duplicated primary keys.
  • Quarantine negative operating baselines, impossible FTE values, and missing owner fields.
  • Confirm salary-cap overages are isolated from FC40 award spending.
  • Confirm frozen fiscal histories are not overwritten by forecast scenarios.
  • Block small-cell demographic or casework slices before JSON reaches the browser.
  • Record reviewer, timestamp, failed rule, and closeout action for every rejected record.

Client-Side Data Resilience — Missing-Value and Render Guardrails
Production-readiness fix · defensive JavaScript architecture
Missing-value states now resolve to governed validation notes, not broken dashboard text
This layer documents how the interactive dashboard prevents missing keys, delayed data loads, malformed rows, and unsafe nested property access from leaking into executive-facing charts, popups, tables, or AI/ML forecast panels.
Optional chainingNullish fallbackSanitized rowsShadow-system governancek<5 suppressionGated drill-throughHuman-in-loop forecasts
Safe property accessMetric reads use optional chaining and nullish coalescing so missing nested values short-circuit safely and receive a controlled fallback before display.
Sanitized ingestionRaw rows are normalized into typed structures before any calculation, Chart.js dataset, table row, or popup receives them.
Lazy render lifecycleCharts queue until the active tab is visible, then render through a visibility observer. Hidden panels no longer trigger Chart.js width/height collisions during rapid tab switching.
Presentation-layer auditA lightweight observer replaces accidental missing-value text with governed validation language and skips code/preformatted examples.
Shadow-system intake registerUnmapped keys, duplicate transfers, stale extracts, and spreadsheet overrides are logged as source-owner issues before they can shape executive metrics.
Privacy-by-constructionGranular salary, vacancy, adjustment, and demographic slices are suppressed when cohort size falls below k<5 or when intersecting dimensions could reconstruct an individual record.
Human-in-loop forecastingWeighted multi-factor, survival, and payroll burn-velocity outputs remain scenario signals; they cannot approve staffing, pay, funding, or policy action.
1. Raw payloadCSV / JSON / semantic-layer response enters with unknown completeness.
2. SanitizeRows are converted into safe text, numbers, arrays, and null chart points.
3. ValidateRequired keys, ranges, owners, refresh dates, and cohort-size rules are checked.
4. RenderChart/table functions are blocked if data is empty, late, invalid, or the target panel is not visible.
5. ExplainAny unresolved value becomes a source-owner validation note, not raw technical output.

Statistical, Privacy, Visualization, and Pipeline Upgrade Path
Use this section as the reviewer-facing audit trail for how the synthetic dashboard would become a governed enterprise people-analytics product.
BacktestingFormal privacyAPI contractsNarrative controls

WMAF production model

Move from static weights to probabilistic survival modeling. Use Cox PH or RSF to estimate the probability of exit by time window while accounting for tenure, engagement decay, compensation pressure, job family, funding source, vacancy pressure, and market conditions.

Target: P(exit by time t | cohort features) + hazard ratio + confidence interval

Validation transparency

Expose MAPE for payroll forecasts, C-index for attrition ranking, calibration plots for observed vs. predicted rates, and model-drift alerts. Display validation status beside the dashboard forecast, not hidden in technical notes.

Publish: model version + training window + backtest error + owner signoff

External pressure vectors

Add local CPI-U, regional wage premium, and role-family market pressure as engineered features. Separate external labor-market pressure from internal management signals so recommendations are not over-attributed to internal climate alone.

Market Pressure = local wage premium + CPI-U trend + role-family demand signal

Privacy by construction

Protect against dimensional intersection and subtraction attacks by enforcing k-anonymity across combined slicers and complementary suppression whenever one hidden value could be reconstructed from totals.

If cohort_n < 5: mask primary cell + mask companion cell or aggregate upward before display

Visualization architecture

Use dot plots, diverging bars, and confidence bands for linear executive comparison. Avoid radar charts for unrelated dimensions. Standardize chart containers with fluid aspect-ratio wrappers for responsive executive review.

.chart-container { width:100%; position:relative; aspect-ratio:16/9; }

Production narrative layer

Generate summaries only from validated semantic-layer JSON. Use strict Zod/Pydantic-style API contracts, dbt semantic-layer checks, data lineage, retrieval-limited prompts, and zero-hallucination rules before publishing narrative text.

API contract → validated metrics JSON → frozen snapshot → governed narrative → audit log

BI Implementation Blueprint — WMAF Scripts, School Risk Parameters & Validation Controls

Power BI / Tableau implementation layer

This layer makes the WMAF model operational for a Dean, CFO, CHRO, HRBP, or Chan School leadership review. The scripts below are turnkey starting points; in production, the measures should be governed by HR, Finance, DEIB, and data-owner approval before publication.

Power BI DAX calculated measure

ProjectedAttrition12M =
VAR CurrentHeadcount =
    COUNTROWS(FILTER('Workforce', 'Workforce'[PositionStatus] = "Filled"))
VAR FY26VolRate = [FY26_Voluntary_Turnover_Rate]
VAR FY25VolRate = [FY25_Voluntary_Turnover_Rate]
VAR FY26InvolRate = [FY26_Involuntary_Turnover_Rate]
VAR Alpha =
    (0.5 * FY26VolRate) +
    (0.3 * FY25VolRate) +
    (0.2 * FY26InvolRate)
VAR BaseHistoricalAttrition = CurrentHeadcount * Alpha
VAR RetirementPipeline =
    COUNTROWS(FILTER('Workforce', 'Workforce'[IsRetirementEligible12M] = TRUE))
VAR ClimateRiskAdjustment =
    COUNTROWS(FILTER('Workforce', 'Workforce'[EngagementScore] < 65)) * 0.15
RETURN
    BaseHistoricalAttrition + RetirementPipeline + ClimateRiskAdjustment

Tableau / TabPy vectorized function

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def calculate_wmaf(headcount, fy26_vol, fy25_vol, fy26_invol,
                   retirement_count, low_engagement_count):
    alpha = (
        0.5 * np.array(fy26_vol) +
        0.3 * np.array(fy25_vol) +
        0.2 * np.array(fy26_invol)
    )
    base_attrition = np.array(headcount) * alpha
    climate_adjustment = np.array(low_engagement_count) * 0.15
    projected_turnover = (
        base_attrition + np.array(retirement_count) + climate_adjustment
    )
    return projected_turnover.tolist()

SQL alert rule pattern

CASE
  WHEN wmaf_rate >= 0.10 OR projected_attrition_12m >= 80 THEN 'High WMAF risk'
  WHEN engagement_score IS NULL THEN 'Missing survey mapping'
  WHEN respondent_count < 5 THEN 'Suppress - privacy threshold'
  WHEN salary_gap_pct >= 0.12 THEN 'High salary review exposure'
  WHEN days_open >= 60 AND job_family IN ('Technology & Data','Research Administration','Finance','Compliance / Risk') THEN 'Aged critical open role'
END AS alert_issue

    "Issue", "Projected attrition above threshold",

  ), NOT ISBLANK([Severity])),
  FILTER(SELECTCOLUMNS('Workforce',
    "Issue", "Salary review exposure",
    "Severity", IF('Workforce'[salary_gap_pct] >= .12, "High", BLANK())
  ), NOT ISBLANK([Severity]))
)

📊 Engagement score

Engagement is modeled as a 0–100 index using anonymized pulse dimensions. Unit scores are weighted averages of business partner support, workload balance, belonging, clarity, and growth opportunity.

Unit engagement = Σ(dimension score × dimension weight) / Σ(weights)
Overall engagement = Σ(unit engagement × active records) / Σ(active records)
Point change = current score − prior-year score

👥 Portfolio, open/pending & active rate

Position portfolio, active records, and open/pending items are modeled at the record level. Open/Pending rate and fill rate should be calculated from the authorized position register, not from budget totals alone.

Open/pending roles = Position portfolio − Filled positions
Filled rate = Filled positions / Position portfolio
Vacancy / pending rate = Open roles / Position portfolio

🤝 Casework and policy risk scoring

Risk levels are based on a point model that weighs severity, days open, partner involvement, employee/service impact, repeat pattern, and documentation quality.

Risk score = severity points + aging points + partner/escalation points + repeat-pattern points + documentation-gap points
High ≥ 75 · Medium 45–74 · Low / monitor < 45

💵 Budget vs. forecast payroll

Forecast payroll is derived from raw position rows. Active service/role records use current salary plus projected adjustment; open/pending records use the budgeted salary adjusted by expected start date and leave/hiring bridge offset assumptions.

Filled forecast = current salary × (1 + projected adjustment %)
Open / Pending forecast = budget salary × active-months factor + leave/hiring bridge offset
Variance = budget salary − forecast salary

📉 WMAF turnover, attrition & retirement forecast

The refined formula separates historical base attrition, known retirement pipeline, and climate/workload stress. It is a planning model for workforce continuity, budget, service-risk, and leadership discussion—not an employee-level prediction tool.

Projected Attrition T_next = Σ(Hᵢ × αᵢ) + R₁₂ + C₁₂
αᵢ = 0.5×Voluntary Rate_FY26 + 0.3×Voluntary Rate_FY25 + 0.2×Involuntary Rate_FY26
R₁₂ = known retirement pipeline within 12 months
C₁₂ = roles with engagement score <65 × 0.15

🧭 Formula-bound final-review values

Final executive values should be bound to live model measures instead of typed into narrative text. This prevents approval-cycle or compensation-exposure contradictions between the KPI cards, executive summary, and drill-down pages.

Median_Approval_Cycle_Label = FORMAT([Median Approval Cycle], "0.0") & " weeks"
Comp_Exposure_Pct = DIVIDE([Count_No_Salary_Review_18M], [Total_Filled_Positions], 0)
Comp_Exposure_Label = FORMAT([Comp_Exposure_Pct], "0.00%") & " of " & FORMAT([Total_Filled_Positions], "#,##0") & " filled positions"

🧪 Survey validation schema

Survey-based engagement and belonging metrics should not load directly into leadership visuals until a validation pass confirms unit mapping, cycle match, respondent count, response rate, range checks, and suppression rules.

Survey_Row_Status = valid only if Unit_ID mapped + Survey_Cycle current + Respondent_Count ≥ 5 + Response_Rate ≥ 30% + no suppressed fields exposed
Missing_Survey_Flag = active filled headcount > 0 and no survey row for selected cycle

🏛️ Dean drill-down design

The Dean view should start with a five-second school scorecard and move progressively into risk drivers, budget impact, DEIB/belonging context, and action ownership. Raw registers should be drill-through, not default landing visuals.

Landing page = School KPIs + Top 3 risks + action due dates
Drill path = School → Tub / Division → Department → Job family / Grade → Position register evidence
Security = dean-visible aggregate + HR/Finance-controlled detail pages

⚖️ Compensation and benchmark references

Benchmark rows are contextual planning inputs. Official salary setting should anchor to Harvard grade/range, internal equity, comparator roles, current postings, and Compensation review.

Market midpoint = (public low + public high) / 2 when available
Internal equity flag = same role / grade spread > 15% or below planning benchmark
Benchmark context ≠ salary recommendation

🧩 Salary range reconciliation logic

Grade range, advertised hiring range, budget salary, current salary, and forecast salary are related but not interchangeable. The dashboard now treats mismatches as a governance signal that requires source-system reconciliation.

Range check = advertised range low/high vs. current salary and budget salary
Budget variance = forecast salary − budget salary
Mismatch status = Review Required when grade range is missing, current salary is outside band, or forecast exceeds approved budget by threshold
Owner = HR Compensation + Finance + Talent Acquisition / hiring manager

🗂️ ARIeS / ATS shortlist integration logic

Shortlist popups should use only authorized recruiting-system fields and role-based access. Academic searches may use ARIeS where applicable; administrative staff searches should use the relevant Careers@Harvard / applicant-tracking workflow. Candidate names and comments must remain restricted on executive views.

Join key = requisition_id + position_id + posting_id
Allowed fields = candidate_stage, internal/external source, finalist flag, selection rationale, offer status, disposition date
Executive view = counts + source mix + masked comments
Secure drill-through = named shortlist only for authorized HR/search users

⏳ 5 / 10 / 15 / 20-year scenarios

Long-range scenarios scale from the current service item portfolio baseline using illustrative assumptions for service demand, review / succession exposure, future-skills shift, and salary-budget growth.

Projected portfolio = baseline portfolio + demand-growth assumption
Review / succession exposure = age/role tenure eligibility estimate × horizon factor
Succession coverage = roles with named backup / critical roles
Budget scenario = salary baseline × inflation / merit / role-growth factors

Scoring rubric used in popups

Risk point guide

  • Severity: 0–30 points based on employee, policy, operational, or reputational impact.
  • Aging: 0–20 points based on days open or urgency window.
  • Pattern: 0–15 points for repeat signals in one unit or job family.
  • Exposure: 0–20 points for finance, service-continuity, policy, or service impact.
  • Control gap: 0–15 points for missing documentation, owner, or next action.

Interpretation thresholds

  • High: ≥75 points; needs dated action, owner, and escalation path.
  • Medium: 45–74 points; needs monitoring plus unit leader / partner action.
  • Monitor: below 45 points; keep in trend view or next scheduled review.
  • Engagement: below 65 = intervention zone; 65–74 = watch; 75+ = stable / strength.
Compliance & Liquidity Safety-Gate Methodology — Grant Commitments, Pledges, ECC & Vacation Accrual
Committed Cost-Share ReserveΣ(Total award value × required institutional match %) creates the legally bound reserve that reduces flexible operating liquidity.
Active Cash-Flow Deficit ExposureCurrent project expenses incurred − liquid cash installments received separates booked pledge value from money available to spend.
Effort Variance Threshold|Payroll direct charge % − certified system effort %| flags any grant payroll movement above the 5% tolerance for research-administration review.
Terminal Vacation LiabilityΣ(unused vacation hours × current hourly pay rate) − central pool subsidy allowance identifies whether the fringe reserve protects local departments.

Governed operating interpretation

These formulas are displayed in methodology because they are control logic, not executive decoration. Production deployment should connect the measures to sponsored-award records, pledge schedules, ECC / effort certification systems, HR leave balances, and fund-accounting controls before any budget action is approved.

source-system reconciliationhuman approval requiredaudit trail preservedno confidential employee data in demo
Advanced Ledger-Control Methodology — Fringe, IP Royalty, Clinical Billing & Endowment Fences
Fringe True-Up ImpactActual fringe expenditures − Σ(salaries × provisional fringe rate) creates the under/over-recovery amount that can surface as a two-year-lag personnel-budget adjustment.
Net Distributable RoyaltyGross licensing revenue − unamortized patent legal costs determines the balance available for inventor, lab, department, and school-core allocation.
Clinical Double-Billing Risk FlagSponsored-project charge ∩ active clinical registry billing code creates an invoice quarantine gate before grant or insurance billing release.
Endowment Health IndexCurrent market value ÷ historical gift principal identifies funds that require payout throttling or payroll fallback planning when the ratio approaches 1.00.

Advanced control interpretation

These ledger controls are intentionally positioned as methodology references and clickable Budget Run-Rate safety gates. They should not crowd the executive dashboard, but they give reviewers a governed audit path from the headline action to the underlying formula, source-system evidence, threshold, and recommended blocker.

FY+2 fringe lagOTD netting before distributionclinical invoice quarantineUPMIFA-style principal fence
Operational Latency & Global Compliance Methodology — CAS, Process Drag, Shared Clusters & NRA Surcharges
CAS Exception ExposureΣ(administrative expenses charged to FC40 without an active OSP/CAS exception flag) isolates auditable direct-charge exposure before salary relief is accepted in the forecast.
Latency-Adjusted Burn VelocityTarget burn rate × [1 − (systemic transaction-day latency ÷ 365)] prevents delayed hiring or procurement from being mislabeled as structural savings.
Shared Cluster SurchargeTotal cluster overhead × (local department transaction volume ÷ total aggregate cluster transaction volume) rebalances finance/HR shared-service costs by actual consumption.
NRA Unfunded Tax LiabilityΣ(gross fellow stipend disbursed × withholding-rate variance) creates the local unrestricted reserve need when international treaty status changes or expires.

Seven-layer FP&A architecture coverage check

The dashboard now separates the executive scan from the governed mechanics across strategy core, operational pillars, mission economics, data infrastructure, compliance bridges, advanced ledger controls, and operational-latency safeguards. The finance tab surfaces only decision-ready blockers; the formulas and audit path remain available through popups and this methodology layer.
